Part 1 — Operator wiki & help handbook

Task-oriented help: how to run every module, day to day.

Smart Hospital — Wiki & Operator Handbook

Practical, task-oriented help for the Smart Hospital hospital-management system (demo.smart-hospital.in). Written from a live exploration of the demo hospital Smart Hospital & Research Center — every workflow below was performed against the running application. Screenshots are in docs/assets/screens/; the screen-by-screen reference is in FEATURE-CATALOG.md.

1. Getting started

1.1 Signing in

Portal URL Who uses it
Admin panel /site/login All hospital staff (9 roles)
Patient portal /site/userlogin Patients (self-service)
Public website / Visitors, prospective patients
  1. Open /site/login.
  2. Enter Username (e-mail address) and Password, click Sign In.
  3. You land on the dashboard for your role. The bell icon, quick-add launcher and global patient search are always available.
  4. Forgot Password? → /site/forgotpassword (patient portal: /site/ufpassword).

On the demo build the login page also offers Quick demo login buttons that fill the credentials for each role.

Role Demo user Password

Admin jason@gmail.com password

1.2 The application shell

  • Sidebar — every module, grouped into five sections: Core Operations, Clinical, Administration, Tools & Content, Reports & Setup. Type in Filter Menu to find a screen by name.
  • Global patient search — the "Search By Patient Name" box in the header searches the whole patient index from any screen and opens the patient profile.
  • Quick Add — floating launcher with Add Patient, New OPD Patient, New IPD Patient, New Appointment, New Bill.
  • Bed status — live bed/ward occupancy modal.
  • Notifications — bell menu with module alerts (OPD/IPD/pathology/radiology/pharmacy/appointment), notices, chat and calendar/to-do.
  • Language switcher and user menu (profile, password, logout).

1.3 The dashboard

The dashboard is role-aware. For a Super Admin it shows:

  • KPI tiles — Total revenue MTD, Bed occupancy, Today's appointments, Outstanding bills, Medicines stock, Blood bank inventory.
  • Yearly income & expense — 12-month trend (collected vs spent).
  • Monthly income overview — donut of income share by module (OPD, IPD, Pharmacy, Pathology, Radiology, Blood Bank, Ambulance, Income).
  • Recent activity — tail of the audit log (bills posted, patients registered…) with user, module, amount and timestamp.
  • Staff attendance — role-wise present/absent summary for the day.
  • Income by module — table with this-month vs last-month comparison.

2. Initial configuration (do this once, as Super Admin)

Recommended order — later modules depend on earlier masters:

  1. Settings (/schsettings) — hospital name, logo, address, contact, currency, date format, time zone, session timeout.
  2. Hospital Charges (/admin/charges) — the charge catalogue used by billing, OPD and IPD (consultation, procedure, room, investigation, etc.).
  3. Bed (/admin/setup/bed/status) — wards, bed groups and individual beds; drives admission and the bed-status board.
  4. Print Header Footer (/admin/printing) — per-module header/footer used on bills, reports, prescriptions, certificates.
  5. Finance (/admin/incomehead) — income and expense heads.
  6. Front Office (/admin/visitorspurpose) — visitor purposes, call log types, complaint types.
  7. Operations (/admin/operationtheatre/index) — operation theatre master.
  8. Pharmacy (/admin/medicinecategory/medicine) — medicine categories, units, suppliers and medicines.
  9. Pathology (/admin/pathologycategory/addcategory) — test categories and tests (with parameters, ranges, units).
  10. Radiology (/admin/lab/addlab) — imaging categories and studies.
  11. Blood Bank (/admin/bloodbank/products) — components, bag types and stock.
  12. Symptoms / Findings / Vitals / ICD-10 — the clinical libraries used by OPD and IPD.
  13. Finance → Referral commission, Human Resource → Leave types, Appointment → slots / online appointment, Inventory → item categories, Custom Fields.
  14. Users & roles: create staff (HR → Add Staff) and assign the role that decides the menu they see.
  15. Notification settings — per-event delivery over e-mail, SMS, WhatsApp and mobile-app push (System Settings → Notification Setting), plus the SMS Setting and Email Setting gateway credentials. See §6.2.
  16. Two-Factor Authentication — 2FA setup for privileged staff (§9.2) using Google Authenticator.
  17. Zoom setting (/admin/zoom_conference) if you will use teleconsultation.
  18. Front CMS (/admin/front/page) to publish the public website.

Tip — Most masters are ordinary list screens: DataTables search, an Add button opening a modal, row actions for edit/delete, and CSV/print export.

3. Front-desk workflows

3.1 Register a patient

Patient → Patient List (/admin/admin/search) → Add New Patient (or Quick Add → Add Patient).

Capture at minimum: name, guardian name, gender, date of birth/age, mobile, e-mail, address, blood group, marital status, photo and (optionally) TPA/insurance details. The system assigns the patient ID (MR number) that every other module uses.

  • Import Patient — bulk import from CSV.
  • Disabled Patient List — archive/restore patients instead of deleting.
  • Delete Selected — bulk delete with the row checkboxes.

3.2 Book an appointment

Appointment (/admin/appointment/index) with tabs Today, Upcoming, Old.

  1. Add Appointment → choose patient (or New Patient), doctor, date, slot, priority and message.
  2. Slots come from Setup → Appointment (/admin/onlineappointment/index); the Doctor Wise view shows a doctor's day.
  3. Queue view prints/serves tokens for walk-ins.
  4. Online bookings made from the public site arrive in Setup → Appointment → Online Appointment for approval.
  5. Change status from the row (booked → confirmed → checked-in → consulted → cancelled).

3.3 OPD visit (out-patient)

OPD – Out Patient (/admin/patient/search) with tabs Today OPD, Upcoming OPD, Old OPD, Patient View.

  1. Select a patient or Add Patient, then New Visit.
  2. In the visit form record: appointment/date, consultant, symptoms (from the symptom library), ICD-10 diagnosis, findings, vitals, history, prescription rows, investigation orders and charges.
  3. Save & Print produces the prescription; Save returns to the list.
  4. Investigations ordered here appear in Pathology/Radiology billing and reporting queues.
  5. Discharge an OPD patient when the episode is complete (vendor help: How to Discharge patient from OPD).

3.4 IPD admission → discharge (in-patient)

IPD – In Patient (/admin/patient/ipdsearch).

  1. New IPD Patient → patient, consultant, ward/bed (from the bed master), admission date, TPA/insurance, guardian and case details.
  2. Inside the case you get tabs for Visit/Overview, Vitals (with BMI), Prescription, Lab Investigation, Radiology, Pharmacy, Billing, Timeline, and specialty blocks such as previous obstetric / postnatal / antenatal history.
  3. Nursing staff record vitals and notes from the same case (their role restricts them to ward work).
  4. Bed transfer and discharge summary are available from the case; discharge frees the bed and unlocks the final IPD bill and certificates.

3.5 Billing & payments

Billing (/admin/bill/dashboard).

  • Single Module Billing — bill one department (OPD, pharmacy, pathology, radiology, blood bank, ambulance…).
  • OPD/IPD billing through Case ID — pull all charges booked against a case.
  • Take full or part payment, choose the payment mode (cash, cheque, card, UPI/bank transfer, TPA), apply discount, then Print the receipt or PDF it.
  • Outstanding amounts roll up into the dashboard tile Outstanding bills and the Unpaid / Overdue split.

3.6 Visitors, calls, post and complaints

Front Office (/admin/visitors) — four registers:

  • Visitor pass — purpose, name, "visit to" (IPD/OPD/staff), phone, ID proof, in/out time.
  • Phone Call Log — incoming/outgoing, caller, related patient, follow-up date.
  • Postal — dispatch and receive register.
  • Complain — complaint type, source, complainant, date, action taken, assigned to.

Purpose lists and call/complaint types are configured in Setup → Front Office (/admin/visitorspurpose).

4. Clinical services

4.1 Pharmacy

Pharmacy (/admin/pharmacy/bill) is the point of sale and store control.

  • Add medicines in Setup → Pharmacy first (category, unit, supplier, batch, MRP, sale price, GST, reorder level).
  • Bill — search a medicine, pick the batch (expiry shown), quantity, discount; the system deducts stock and posts the income to the dashboard.
  • Stock / Bad stock — receive purchase, transfer between store and counter, mark expiry/bad stock (vendor help: How to add Medicine Stock / Bad Stock).
  • Import Medicines — CSV import for large catalogues.
  • Returns and refunds are handled from the bill list.

4.2 Pathology (laboratory)

Pathology (/admin/pathology/gettestreportbatch).

  1. Order tests against a patient (or accept an OPD/IPD order).
  2. Sample collection → result entry per parameter (value, unit, normal range) → approve/verify.
  3. Generate report — single or batch (many patients at once), with configured header/footer and print/PDF output.
  4. Payment for tests is posted to billing; the Pathology Bill screen tracks it.

4.3 Radiology (imaging)

Radiology (/admin/radio/gettestreportbatch) — same order → schedule → perform → report flow, with findings/impression text and attachments. Reports print in batch like pathology.

4.4 Blood bank

Blood Bank (/admin/bloodbankstatus/).

  • Stock — component-wise (Whole blood, PRBC, FFP, platelets) and group-wise (A+, B+, O-, AB+ …) with bag numbers and expiry.
  • Donor registry — donor details, screening, donation history.
  • Issue — issue to a patient (with cross-match), record return or discard.
  • Dashboard tile and alerts keep an eye on low stock.

4.5 Ambulance

Ambulance (/admin/vehicle/getcallambulance) — vehicle and driver master, call register (caller, patient, pickup address, date/time), charge for the trip and status (pending → dispatched → completed).

5. Administration & human resources

5.1 Staff and HR

Human Resource (/admin/staff) — staff directory with Staff ID, name, role, department, designation, mobile, photo.

  • Add Staff — personal and professional details, role (drives permissions), login credentials, payroll and leave policy.
  • Card View / List View toggle.
  • From a staff record: Staff Attendance, Payroll, Leaves.

5.2 QR-code attendance

QR Code Attendance → Attendance (/admin/qrattendance/attendance/index) shows the monthly register (present/absent/half-day/late, in and out time).

  • Settings (/admin/qrattendance/setting/index) configures the QR/check-in window and rules; staff scan the hospital QR to mark attendance.
  • Attendance feeds the dashboard Staff attendance panel and HR reports.

5.3 Duty roster and calendar

  • Duty Roster (/admin/dutyroster/roster_report) — assign shifts (morning/evening/night) per staff and department, per day; export/print the roster.
  • Annual Calendar (/admin/holiday/index) — holidays, events and (per vendor help) to-do items.

5.4 Birth & death register

Birth Record (/admin/birthordeath) and Death Record (/admin/birthordeath/death) capture the statutory fields (child/parent details, hospital, doctor, certificate number) and print certificates. Both feed the Birth Death report.

5.5 Referral commissions

Referral (/admin/referral/payment) — referral doctor/agent master, commission percentage per service (Setup → Referral), and the ledger of commission payable/paid per referred case.

5.6 TPA / insurance

TPA Management (/admin/tpamanagement) — insurance companies, TPA master, patient policies and claim status tracking; TPA payments appear in the TPA report and in billing as a payment mode.

5.7 Finance ledger

  • Income (/admin/income) and Expenses (/admin/expense) — head-wise entries with date, amount, invoice/reference, remark and attachment.
  • Heads are maintained in Setup → Finance (/admin/incomehead).
  • Both feed the Finance report, the dashboard trend chart and Income by module.

5.8 Multi-branch

Multi Branch has three screens:

  • Overview (/admin/multibranch/branch/overview) — group KPIs per branch (patients, collections, beds) side by side.
  • Report (/admin/multibranch/branch/report) — comparative reporting across branches.
  • Settings (/admin/multibranch/branch) — the branch master (name, code, address, contact, admin) plus the branch switcher in the header.

6. Communication, content and documents

6.1 Notice board / messaging

Messaging (/admin/notification) — publish notices to selected audiences (roles, staff, patients, branch) with title, message, date, attachment and publish/expiry window. Recipients see them in the bell menu.

6.2 Notifications, SMS, e-mail and WhatsApp

Notifications are event driven. For each event (for example OPD Patient Registration, IPD Patient Discharge, Appointment Approved, Login Credentials) you choose which channels deliver it:

Channel Where it is configured Notes
System / in-app System Settings → Notification Setting Bell menu + notice board
E-mail Email Setting (SMTP credentials) Used for credentials and reports
SMS SMS Setting (gateway credentials) Charged per message by the gateway
WhatsApp WhatsApp Messaging → Meta (Cloud API) or Twilio One provider at a time; the template configured for the event is used
Mobile app push Android app integration Free channel for installed patients/staff

WhatsApp setup — open WhatsApp Messaging, choose the Meta tab (official WhatsApp Business Cloud API) or the Twilio tab (sandbox or approved sender), enter the credentials, enable exactly one provider, then switch WhatsApp on per event on the Notification Setting page. The same event template that already goes out by e-mail/SMS is reused. Mirror: docs/help-library/whatsapp-messaging/.

Patient credentials can be sent from the patient record over any enabled channel (e-mail/SMS/WhatsApp/push), which is how patients get access to the patient panel (see §8).

6.3 Survey forms

Survey Forms (/admin/survey) — build questionnaires (question types: text, textarea, radio, checkbox, dropdown, date, rating), publish them to selected roles/departments and read responses. My Survey Forms (/admin/survey/staff_forms) is the staff-facing list of forms assigned to the signed-in user.

6.4 Download center

Download Center (/admin/content/upload, /admin/content/list, /admin/contenttype/) — content types, upload/share files (reports, circulars, policies) with audience and download counters.

6.5 Certificates and ID cards

  • Certificate (/admin/generatecertificate) — choose module (OPD/IPD), discharged patients and a certificate template; generate single or multiple at once and print.
  • Patient ID Card (/admin/generatepatientidcard/) and Staff ID Card (/admin/generatestaffidcard/) — template-based cards with photo, ID and validity.

6.6 Inventory

Inventory (/admin/itemstock) — item categories (Setup → Inventory), suppliers, item master, issue/return to departments, stock ledger and reorder alerts; Inventory report shows consumption.

6.7 Front CMS (public website)

Front CMS (/admin/front/page) manages the public site: pages, banners/sliders, news & events, gallery, departments, doctors, contact and SEO metadata. Content published here appears on the hospital website and in the "What's new" block of the login page.

6.8 Telemedicine

  • Live Consultation (/admin/zoom_conference/consult) — schedule a Zoom teleconsultation for a patient, share the join link, start/end the session; the call is logged for reporting.
  • Live Meeting (/admin/zoom_conference/meeting) — internal staff meetings with participants and schedule.
  • Configure Zoom keys/secret in Setup → Zoom Setting (/admin/zoom_conference).

7. Reports

Reports menu (17 report screens in the admin UI). Every report shares the same pattern: date range + module-specific filters → Search → results table → export/print.

The vendor help library documents 44 report articles (per-report how-tos such as Daily Transaction Report, Stock Report, Balance Amount Report, Pathology/Radiology Balance Report). They are mirrored under docs/help-library/reports/ and indexed in docs/HELP-LIBRARY.md.

Report What you get
Finance Collections, income vs expense, payment-mode wise summary
Appointment Bookings by period, doctor, status
OPD Visit counts, diagnosis mix, doctor-wise load
IPD Admissions, discharges, bed-days, ward-wise census
Pharmacy Sales, stock movement, expiry/bad stock, profit
Pathology Test-wise counts, revenue, pending vs reported
Radiology Study counts and revenue
Blood Bank Donations, issues, component stock
Ambulance Calls, trips, revenue
Birth Death Birth and death register extracts
Human Resource Staff list, attendance, leaves, payroll
TPA Claim-wise and company-wise settlement status
Inventory Item consumption and stock valuation
Live Consultation Teleconsultation log and duration
OT Operation theatre utilisation and procedures
Patient Patient demographics and registration trend
Log System audit trail (user, module, action, record, time)

8. Patient portal & public website

  • Patient portal (/site/userlogin) — patients sign in with the credentials sent from the patient record and get their own dashboard (counts per module plus charts of medical history, findings and symptoms). Sections available to the patient:
  • My Appointments — view and book an appointment (date, specialist, doctor, shift, slot, priority, message, live-consultation option).
  • OPD — visits list; open a visit for overview, visits, charges, payment, lab investigations, timeline, medication, operation theatre and live consultation.
  • IPD — overview, nurse notes, consultant register, lab investigations, timeline, prescription, charges, payment, treatment history, medication, operation theatre, live consultation and bed history.
  • Pharmacy / Pathology / Radiology / Blood Bank / Ambulance — bill and payment history per module, printable bills and payment receipts.
  • Live Consultation — join the Zoom teleconsultation booked from appointment, OPD or IPD.
  • Reference: docs/help-library/patient-panel/.
  • Public website — driven by Front CMS: home page with departments, doctors, services, health packages, news, gallery, contact and an online appointment form. Online bookings land in the admin Online Appointment queue.
  • New patient registration on the public site creates a patient record that appears in the admin Patient List with the same MR number.

9. Roles, permissions and security

9.1 Roles and the audit trail

  • Nine staff roles ship by default; each role maps to a permission set that controls the sidebar and every screen.
  • The signed-in role is shown in the header (e.g. Super ADMIN); switching role requires re-login.
  • Every form carries a CSRF token; passwords are hashed; sessions expire per the configured timeout.
  • The Log report and dashboard Recent activity give an audit trail of who did what and when.
  • The Android app (vendor addon) provides the same staff/patient flows on mobile with push notifications; see docs/help-library/changelog/ and backlog E13 for mobile coverage.
  • Vendor documentation covers SSL enablement, LAN deployment, and moving the installation between servers.

9.2 Two-factor authentication

The product ships a Two Factor Authentication module (Google Authenticator / TOTP):

  1. Sign in as Super Admin (or the staff member) and open Two Factor Authentication → Setup 2FA.
  2. Install Google Authenticator (or any TOTP app) on the mobile device.
  3. Scan the QR code (or manually enter the key shown in the module) and confirm the 6-digit code to finish enrolment.
  4. From then on, sign-in asks for the current code in addition to the password.
  5. To reset a lost device, delete the 2FA account for that user from the same module and re-enrol.
  6. If automatic enrolment fails, the key for superadmin/staff can be configured manually (vendor article).

Mirror: docs/help-library/two-factor-authentication/. Recommendation for DiziHospital: enforce 2FA for every role that can reach billing or clinical records (backlog E4).

10. Troubleshooting & FAQ

Symptom What to check
Cannot log in / login URL missing Correct portal (/site/login vs /site/userlogin); see vendor article Unable to Login or Missing Login URL.
A menu item is missing for a user Their role does not include that permission — adjust the role/staff record.
Blank page or 500 error ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY SQL mode on the MySQL server (vendor article), or missing PHP extensions (mysqli, mbstring, zip, curl).
"404 / Page not found" after installation mod_rewrite disabled or .htaccess missing (vendor article 404 Or Page Not Found Error In Installation).
Reports return no rows Date range, branch filter and module status filters are cumulative — widen the range first.
Stock not decreasing in pharmacy The bill must be paid/saved, not merely drafted; bad/expired stock uses the Bad Stock entry.
Lab report not printable Results must be approved/verified before the report can be generated.
Patient portal shows no investigations Reports are visible to the patient only after they are released/approved.
Slow pages Enable caching/CDN, check server resources; PHP max_execution_time ≥ 60s is recommended by the vendor.
Need a field that does not exist Add it non-invasively through Setup → Custom Fields.

Frequently asked (vendor articles, for depth): multi-hospital usage, running on a local LAN without internet, moving to a new server, enabling SSL, special characters, adding calendar events and to-dos, chat contacts.

11. Glossary

Term Meaning
OPD Out-Patient Department — walk-in/consultation visits
IPD In-Patient Department — admitted patients
MR / Patient ID Master record number identifying a patient across modules
Case ID The episode identifier linking OPD/IPD visits, orders and bills
TPA Third-Party Administrator handling insurance claims
ICD-10 International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision — diagnosis coding
Charge master Catalogue of billable items and prices
Bad stock Expired/damaged medicine stock written off
Roster Duty/shift plan per staff member
Vitals Temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiration, SpO₂, BMI
Sample collection Pathology step between ordering a test and entering results
Batch A specific lot of a medicine identified by batch number and expiry
MRP / Sale price Maximum retail price / the price charged to the patient
QR attendance Staff attendance marked by scanning a QR code

1.1 The application shell

Every screen sits inside the same shell:

  • Sidebar with a live Filter Menu box, grouped into the five sections above, collapsible sub-menus and per-item icons.
  • Header: Search By Patient Name (global patient index search), the Quick Add launcher (Add Patient · New OPD Patient · New IPD Patient · New Appointment · New Bill), Bed Status board, language switcher, calendar, chat, the notification bell (module alerts) and the user menu (profile, password, sign out).
  • Work area with breadcrumb/page title, DataTables grids (search, sort, paginate, export/print), Bootstrap modals for every add/edit form, and print/PDF output for documents.

2. Modules, screens and forms

2.1 Core Operations

Day-to-day desk work: the dashboard, the master patient index, billing, appointments and the OPD/IPD clinical desks.

Key capabilities

  • One dashboard aggregating revenue, bed occupancy, appointments, stock, blood bank and per-module income share.
  • A single patient master index shared by OPD, IPD, billing, pharmacy, pathology and radiology.
  • Appointment desk with doctor-wise slots, a queue/token view and online-appointment intake.
  • OPD/IPD desks expose the whole clinical record: vitals, symptoms, ICD-10 diagnosis, prescription, lab and radiology orders and a timeline.
# Screen What it covers Path
1 Dashboard Role-aware landing page: KPI tiles (revenue MTD, bed occupancy, appointments, outstanding bills, medicine stock, blood-bank stock), a 12-month income-vs-expense trend, a module-wise income donut, the latest activity feed, staff attendance and module income table. /admin/admin/dashboard
2 Patient List Master patient index. Search, add or import patients, view disabled patients, open the full patient profile and jump straight into a bill. /admin/admin/search
3 Single Module Billing Billing workbench: single-module billing and OPD/IPD billing through a case ID, part payments, payment modes, discounting and printable receipts. /admin/bill/dashboard
4 Appointment Appointment desk with Today / Upcoming / Old tabs, doctor-wise and queue views, slot validation and online-appointment handling. /admin/appointment/index
5 OPD - Out Patient OPD desk: Today / Upcoming / Old visit lists plus the "New Visit" workflow (symptoms, ICD-10, prescription, investigations, charges) and the patient view. /admin/patient/search
6 IPD Patient IPD desk: admission, bed/ward allocation, consultant assignment, daily notes, medication, investigations, charges and discharge. /admin/patient/ipdsearch

2.2 Clinical & Ancillary Services

The departments that raise bills and reports against a patient: pharmacy, laboratory, imaging, blood bank, ambulance and front office.

Key capabilities

  • Pharmacy store and sale workflow with batch, expiry, GST, discount and stock movement.
  • Pathology and radiology: order → sample/procedure → result entry → report generation → print/PDF, single or in batch.
  • Blood-bank stock by component and group, donor registry and issue to patient.
  • Ambulance call register with vehicle/driver assignment and trip charges.
  • Front office covers visitors, phone call logs, postal dispatch and complaints.
# Screen What it covers Path
1 Pharmacy Bill Pharmacy point of sale: batch-wise issue, GST, discounts, stock deduction and printable bill. /admin/pharmacy/bill
2 Pathology Bill Laboratory worklist: order intake, sample collection, result entry/approval and single or batch report generation. /admin/pathology/gettestreportbatch
3 Radiology Bill Imaging worklist: order intake, scheduling, findings entry and batch report generation. /admin/radio/gettestreportbatch
4 Blood Bank Blood bank: component stock by group, donor registry, issue to patient and status board. /admin/bloodbankstatus/
5 Ambulance Call List Ambulance call register with vehicle/driver, trip details and charges. /admin/vehicle/getcallambulance
6 Visitor List Reception toolkit: visitor pass, phone call log, postal register and complaints. /admin/visitors

2.3 Administration & HR

Back office: legal registers, multi-branch operation, staff HR, attendance, rosters, referrals, insurance/TPA and the finance ledger.

Key capabilities

  • Birth and death registers with the fields needed for statutory certificates.
  • Multi-branch console: consolidated overview, branch comparison report and branch master with header switching.
  • HR: staff directory, roles, payroll, leaves, QR-code attendance and duty roster report.
  • Referral commission ledger and TPA/insurance register.
  • Income and expense ledgers that feed the finance reports and the dashboard.

2.4 Communication, Content & Certificates

Everything that talks to people or produces a document: surveys, notice board, downloads, inventory, ID cards, certificates, the public website CMS and telemedicine.

Key capabilities

  • Survey/questionnaire builder with per-role assignment and response collection.
  • Notice board / messaging with audience targeting and attachments.
  • Download center for sharing documents with staff, patients and the public site.
  • Certificate generator plus patient and staff ID cards driven by templates.
  • Front CMS that drives the public hospital website (pages, banners, news, gallery, contact).
  • Zoom-based live consultation and internal live meetings.

1 Survey Forms Survey builder: create questionnaires, assign them to roles/departments and read responses. /admin/survey

3 Notice Board Notice board for staff/patients with audience targeting and attachments. /admin/notification
4 Item Stock List Item stock control: categories, suppliers, issue and return, stock ledger and reorder levels. /admin/itemstock
5 Upload /Share Content Upload/share documents with staff, patients or the public site, with content type and audience. /admin/content/upload

12 Live Consultation Zoom teleconsultation: schedule a session for a patient, share the link, start/end and log the call. /admin/zoom_conference/consult
13 Live Meeting Internal staff video meetings with scheduling and participants. /admin/zoom_conference/meeting

2.5 Reports, Masters & Configuration

The 17 management reports plus the master data and lookups that make the rest of the application work.

Key capabilities

  • Report centre covering finance, appointment, OPD, IPD, pharmacy, pathology, radiology, blood bank, ambulance, birth/death, HR, TPA, inventory, live consultation, operation theatre, patient and the system audit log.
  • Masters for charges, beds, print headers, front-office purposes, operation theatre, pharmacy, pathology, radiology, blood bank, symptoms, ICD-10, findings, vitals, finance heads, leave types, referral commission, appointment slots, inventory items and custom fields.

7. Cross-cutting platform features

Capability What it does
Authentication Separate admin and patient sign-in endpoints (/site/login, /site/userlogin), CSRF token on every form, forgot-password for both portals, password hashing.
Role-based access control Nine staff roles controlling sidebar, screens and reports; role is set on the staff record.
Multi-branch Branch master, branch switching from the header, consolidated overview and cross-branch reporting.
Global patient search Persistent header search over the patient index, available from every screen.
Quick Add launcher Floating launcher for the five most used create actions from anywhere in the app.
Bed status board Live occupancy modal in the header, plus the bed master screen.
Notifications Bell menu with module alerts (OPD/IPD/pathology/radiology/pharmacy/appointment), notice board and chat.
Printing & PDF Bills, receipts, prescriptions, lab/radiology reports, certificates and ID cards, each with a configurable per-module header/footer.
Data grids DataTables on every list: search, sort, pagination, page length and CSV/print/copy export.
Dashboards & analytics KPI tiles, line and donut charts, module income share, staff attendance and activity feed.
Charge master Central catalogue of billable items reused by billing, OPD and IPD.
Clinical libraries Symptoms, findings, vitals, ICD-10 codes and prescription sets shared across clinical screens.
Custom fields Extend core entities with hospital-specific fields from Setup → Custom Fields.
Localisation Language switcher and phrase files (multi-language per vendor documentation).
Communication Notice board, messaging, survey forms, download centre and e-mail/SMS notification settings.
Telemedicine Zoom integration for live consultations and internal meetings.
QR attendance QR-code based staff check-in with roster and holiday calendar.
Audit trail System log report plus the dashboard activity feed (who did what, in which module, when).
Two-factor authentication Optional Google Authenticator (TOTP) 2FA for superadmin and staff: enrol, reset and manual key configuration.
Notification engine Event-driven notifications with per-event channel toggles across in-app, e-mail, SMS, WhatsApp and mobile push.
WhatsApp messaging Patient/staff notifications over WhatsApp via Meta (Cloud API) or Twilio — one provider active at a time, reusing the event template.
Mobile app Vendor Android app for staff and patients with push notifications (documented in the vendor help library, not part of this screen capture).
Patient panel Patient self-service portal: personal dashboard with charts, appointment booking, OPD/IPD history, pharmacy/pathology/radiology/blood-bank/ambulance bills and Zoom live consultation.

Findings from the full application exploration (76 screens, all forms, all roles, public site) and a prioritised plan for the next phase. Every item references evidence: the screenshot id is the file name in docs/assets/screens/.

Priority key — P0 blocking/risky, P1 high value, P2 valuable, P3 nice to have. Size — S ≤ 1 day, M 2–5 days, L 1–3 weeks, XL > 3 weeks.

2. Findings & backlog

2.1 Correctness, trust and data integrity

# Finding (evidence) Why it matters Fix Pri Size
A1 Dashboard tile arithmetic is inconsistent: Bed occupancy 56% vs 30 / 54, and the same card says 24 Available · 30 Allotted · 0 Unused (001-dashboard) Numeric contradictions destroy trust in every other number Centralise KPI computation in one service; add server-side tests for each KPI; show "as of" timestamp P0 M
A2 Mixed currency presentation — the demo shows $ on all money columns (001, 003, 025, 026) while the product is used mostly in INR markets Wrong invoices/reports for the payer Make currency symbol/locale a single setting; format through one helper; add thousand/lakh formatting option P0 S
A3 Outstanding-bills tile shows 171 Unpaid · 67 Overdue but Today's appointments 0 with an empty grid (001, 004) — empty-state vs zero-state are conflated Users cannot tell "no data" from "not loaded" Distinguish empty states with explicit messaging + "why is this empty" hint P1 S
A4 Terminology drift in navigation: "Complain" (should be Complaint), "Overview" vs "Overview ", inconsistent Title Case, "Birth & Death Record" group holding a "Birth Record" duplicate (012, 015, nav.json) Professionalism + searchability Ship a terminology pass + i18n key review P1 S
A5 Duplicated destructive actions: Delete Selected on list screens with no confirmation summary of what will be deleted (002-patient) Accidental loss of clinical records Two-step delete with count preview + soft-delete default + restore view P0 M
A6 Character-encoding defects in the IPD patient header — Â· mojibake and a raw &mdash; entity are printed where separators belong (detail-ipd-profile.jpg) Looks unprofessional on the screen a clinician opens most; same class of bug can corrupt names/addresses Force UTF-8 end to end (PHP output, DB connection charset, HTML meta), escape once only, add a smoke test asserting no raw entities in rendered pages P0 S
A7 A stray literal "2" is rendered as a button/link on almost every list screen (visible in every captured profile, e.g. 002-patient, 018-human-resource) — a badge/count leaking into the DOM as an action label Confusing affordance; screen-reader noise Trace the label (likely a notification count template), give it a proper accessible name or render an icon with aria-label P1 S
A8 Field/column naming typos reach the UI: refference in the OPD/IPD form field names, "Complain" instead of "Complaint" (005, 012) Data exports and integrations inherit the typos Terminology + field-name cleanup pass with a migration-safe alias map P2 S

2.2 Clinical & operational workflow gaps

# Gap Impact Proposal Pri Size
B1 No visible patient queue/token display for waiting rooms; Queue exists inside Appointment only (004) Reception crowding, no patient self-visibility Add a queue/token board screen (TV mode) with live status per doctor/counter P1 M
B2 No bed-transfer / bed-board interaction in the captured UI (058 is a status list) Nurses phone the desk to move patients Drag-and-drop bed board with transfer history and housekeeping status (clean/dirty/blocked) P1 L
B3 Lab workflow has no barcode/specimen tracking or instrument interface (008) Sample mix-ups, manual transcription Specimen barcode + analyzer (HL7/ASTM) interface + critical-value alerting with acknowledgement P1 XL
B4 Discharge summary / OT notes templates are not visible as structured documents (006, 061, 055) Doctors retype; medico-legal risk Template engine with specialty packs, versioning, e-sign and print/PDF P1 L
B5 No consent forms, no patient allergy/interaction checking in pharmacy (007) Patient safety Allergy/intolerance register + interaction warnings at prescription and dispense time P0 L
B6 No appointment reminders or no-show handling visible (004, 029, 004 online queue) Revenue leakage (no-shows ~15–25%) SMS/WhatsApp/e-mail reminder ladder, confirm/decline links, waitlist auto-fill P1 M
B7 Blood bank has stock and issue but no cross-match/antibody record screens captured (010) Transfusion safety Cross-match worksheet, reaction reporting, donor deferral register P1 L
B8 No ambulance dispatch tracking (driver app/GPS) — only a call register (011) Emergency response visibility Live dispatch board + ETA + vehicle status, optional driver mobile link P2 L
B9 No structured referral/transfer-out letter between branches or hospitals (023, 015) Continuity of care Referral document with clinical summary attached to the case P2 M

2.3 Money and billing

# Gap Impact Proposal Pri Size
C1 No online payment capture in the admin billing screens captured (003) Patients must pay at the counter Payment-gateway integration (UPI/card/netbanking) with reconciliation report P1 L
C2 Outstanding/overdue bills have no dunning workflow (001 tile only) Slow collections Ageing buckets, statement generation, reminder schedule, write-off approval flow P1 M
C3 Insurance/TPA is a register, not a claim pipeline (024, 051) Claims delayed/rejected Claim status workflow, document checklist, shortfall tracking, submission log P1 L
C4 No GST/e-invoice compliance artefacts visible on bills (003, 059) Statutory risk in India GST fields per charge head, HSN/SAC, tax invoice format, e-invoice export P2 L
C5 No financial close/period locking or expense approval chain (025, 026) Books can be edited after closing Period close + approval workflow + immutable audit of edits P1 M

2.4 Experience, design and accessibility

# Finding (evidence) Impact Fix Pri Size
D1 76 screens, many list screens with 8–15 near-identical forms in the DOM (all modals pre-rendered: 002 shows 5 forms, 038/039 show 31/34 forms) Slow pages, fragile DOM, hard to maintain Lazy-render modals; split screens; introduce a component library with consistent patterns P1 L
D2 Global patient search matches name only (002, header) Staff cannot find patients by ID/phone (the most reliable identifiers) Extend to MR number, phone, guardian name, with fuzzy match and recent results P0 S
D3 Filter/search controls reset when you return from a record (typical DataTables client-side state) Repetitive work per patient Persist filters in URL/session; remember last view per user P1 M
D4 Accessibility: icon-only controls without accessible names, low-contrast badges/status pills, inconsistent focus outlines, table headers not scoped (observed across all screens) WCAG failure, poor for low-vision staff Accessibility pass: names/roles, contrast tokens, focus rings, scope on headers, modal focus trap P1 M
D5 No keyboard shortcuts or command palette; power users click through menus (sh-sidenav) Slow for heavy users (billing/lab) Command palette (Ctrl-K) + screen shortcuts + barcode/scan-to-search P2 M
D6 No dark mode / high-contrast theme for night shifts (a --sh-theme-vars token block exists but no toggle) Eye strain on night duty Ship theme toggle wired to the existing token layer, honour prefers-color-scheme P2 S
D7 Print/PDF output uses per-module headers; no unified preview (059) Surprise formatting on real paper WYSIWYG print preview + template validation before saving P2 M
D8 Mobile: admin screens are desktop-first (fixed 1440 layout, wide tables) Doctors/nurses work on phones/tablets Responsive table pattern (card mode), touch targets, PWA shell P1 L

2.5 Platform, integration and scale

# Gap Impact Proposal Pri Size
E1 No API layer found for the admin app (server-rendered CodeIgniter views + jQuery) Blocks mobile apps, kiosks, partner integrations Versioned REST/JSON API with token auth, OpenAPI spec, rate limits P1 XL
E2 No webhook/event bus for external systems (029 is a notice board) Cannot integrate with HIS/LIS/PACS/ERP Event outbox (patient.created, bill.paid, report.ready) + webhooks P2 L
E3 Legacy stack (PHP/CodeIgniter + jQuery, vendor-maintained) Hiring and security updates Decide: harden current stack vs. strangler-pattern re-platform; document decision record P1 XL
E4 Security hardening gaps: two-factor authentication exists (Google Authenticator, see docs/help-library/two-factor-authentication/) but is optional and per-user, and there is no password-policy UI, no session/IP register, no login throttling and no forced enrolment for privileged roles (/site/login) Breach and compliance risk Enforce 2FA for Super Admin/Admin and for any role that can see billing or clinical records, add recovery codes, password policy, login throttling, session register and admin action audit P0 L
E11 Notification delivery (e-mail/SMS/WhatsApp/mobile push) is configured per event, but there is no delivery log, retry or failure alerting surfaced in the product (docs/help-library/system-settings/, whatsapp-messaging/) Reminders and credentials silently fail to send Delivery log with status/error per message, automatic retry with backoff, provider failover and a daily failure digest P1 M
E12 WhatsApp is one-way (template notifications); patient replies are not captured into the app Patients reply "CONFIRM"/"cancel" and nothing happens Two-way WhatsApp/webhook inbox linked to the appointment and case, with opt-in/opt-out handling P2 L
E13 The Android app and its push channel are documented by the vendor but not covered by our screen-level catalogue or by any in-repo test Mobile regressions invisible; parity unknown Add the Android app to the coverage map: capture its screens, document feature parity with the web app and add smoke tests P2 L
E5 Vendor licence validation screen in the super-admin shell (001 footer modals: Register your purchase code, Register your Addon) SaaS/productisation blocker; runtime dependency on vendor licence server Replace with first-party licensing/feature flags; make it non-blocking for self-hosted builds P1 M
E6 No observability: no health endpoint, structured logs, metrics or error tracking observed Blind during incidents Health/readiness endpoints, structured audit + app logs, metrics (latency, errors), alerting P1 M
E7 Backup/restore not exposed in the UI (vendor docs cover manual DB backup only) Data-loss risk One-click encrypted backups, retention policy, restore drill, documented RPO/RTO P0 M
E8 No automated tests / CI in the product Regressions on every change Add CI (lint + unit + smoke E2E on the golden-path journeys used for this capture) P1 L
E9 Large datasets: lists are DataTables client-side with default page length 10 (002, 018) Degrades at hospital scale (100k+ patients) Server-side pagination/search, DB indexes, query budgets, caching for dashboards P1 L
E10 India digital-health interoperability (ABDM/ABHA, FHIR) absent Regulatory direction and payer requirements ABHA creation/linking, FHIR R4 facade for key resources, consent artefact handling P2 XL

2.6 Content, portal and communication

# Gap Impact Proposal Pri Size
F1 Patient portal capture shows only login; self-service depth (reports, bills, rebooking) unverified (patient-portal-login.jpg) Adoption of self-service Confirm/extend: download reports, pay bills, rebook, family accounts, notification preferences P2 M
F2 Survey forms are admin-defined; no NPS/feedback trigger after discharge (027, 028) No voice-of-patient loop Auto-send feedback survey after discharge/payment with KPI dashboard P2 M
F3 Notice board/messaging has no read receipts or escalation (029) Policy notices unverified Read tracking, acknowledgement-required notices, escalation P2 S
F4 Front CMS content is strong but has no SEO/schema analytics surface in the capture (037) Lost patient acquisition Health-check for SEO meta, structured data for departments/doctors, analytics hookup P3 S
F5 No patient-facing cost estimate or package pricing on the site/front desk Price anxiety and disputes Package/estimate builder (procedure → expected cost) printable for the patient P2 M

3. Suggested sequence

Phase 1 — Trust & safety (2–3 weeks, P0 items) A1 KPI correctness · A2 currency/locale · A5 safe delete · B5 allergy & interaction checks · D2 smarter patient search · E4 security baseline (MFA, throttle, session register) · E7 backup/restore.

Phase 2 — Front-desk velocity (3–4 weeks, high-value P1) B1 queue board · B6 reminders & no-show recovery · C2 collections ageing + statements · D1 page/modals performance · D3 filter persistence · E9 server-side pagination on the biggest lists (patients, bills, lab).

Phase 3 — Clinical depth (4–6 weeks) B3 lab barcode + analyzer interface · B4 discharge/OT templates · B7 cross-match & reaction reporting · C3 TPA claim pipeline · C1 online payments.

Phase 4 — Platform (ongoing) E1 API layer + E2 webhooks · E10 ABDM/FHIR · E6 observability · E8 CI/test harness · D8 responsive/PWA.

4. Definition of done (shared)

Every item above ships with: acceptance criteria written first, automated test where the layer allows it, documentation updated in this repo (docs/), a screenshot of the new state replacing the old one in docs/assets/screens/, and an entry in docs/CHANGELOG.md.

5.1 About Two Factor Authentication

Vendor article · category: Two Factor Authentication · Sat, 16 Aug, 2025 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/about-two-factor-authentication

2FA, or Two-Factor Authentication, is a security process in which a user is required to provide two different forms of authentication in order to access an account or system. The goal of 2FA is to make it harder for unauthorized individuals to gain access to an account, even if they have obtained the user's password or other credentials.

The two factors of authentication typically used in 2FA are:

  1. Something the user knows, such as a password, PIN, or answer to a security question.
  2. Something the user has, such as a physical token, a one-time code generated by an authentication app, or an SMS code sent to their phone.

When 2FA is enabled for an account, the user must provide both factors of authentication to gain access. For example, they might enter their password as the first factor, and then enter a one-time code generated by an authentication app as the second factor.

By requiring two different factors of authentication, 2FA makes it much more difficult for attackers to gain access to an account. Even if an attacker manages to obtain the user's password, they will still need the second factor of authentication to gain access. This makes it much less likely that an attacker will be able to successfully compromise the account.

5.2 How to Setup 2FA?

Vendor article · category: Two Factor Authentication · Sat, 16 Aug, 2025 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/how-to-setup-2fa

Note: For further processing, you need to set up Google Authenticator on your mobile device.

5.3 How to Install the Google Authenticator app on a mobile device?

Vendor article · category: Two Factor Authentication · Sat, 16 Aug, 2025 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/how-to-install-the-google-authenticator-app-on-a-mobile-device

  1. On your mobile device, go to Play Store / IOS.
  2. Download the Google Authenticator app.
  3. After downloading the app, install in your device.

  1. Now open the Google Authenticator app and setup your first account.
  2. Use the QR code or setup key in your 2FA settings (by Google or third-party service). If you’re having trouble, go to g.co/2sv
  3. Now click on Scan a QR code from your mobile.

  1. Now, scan the QR code, which is available on your Smart Hospital Two Factor Authentication > Setup 2FA page**.**

  1. You will receive the six-digit verification code, which will show up in the Google Authenticator
  2. Now fill in the six-digit verification code below the QR code and click on "Verify and Activate."
  3. You have successfully enabled the 2FA method in your Smart Hospital, and a message will be shown on screen.

  • IPD Patient Registration: IPD Patient

  • Live Consultation: Patient

Note**-**If you are using any Indian SMS gateway then your template content must be match with your DLT registered template content.

5.8 Email Setting

Vendor article · category: System Settings · Tue, 09 Nov, 2021 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/email-setting

After adding student or staff if you found there is no email is sending by system then there may be email configuration issue on your server / Smart Hospital.

In Smart Hospital we have used phpmailer https://github.com/PHPMailer/PHPMailerlibrary which is used by many popular php application like WordPress, Drupal, SugarCRM, Yii, Joomla etc.

By default SendMail is set as Email Engine in Setup > Settings > Email Setting. SendMail can only work and send emails if you cpanel hosting supports it. If SendMail not sending email then contact to your hosting provider. Since SendMail is easiest but less reliable so check email recipient account Spam folder because sometimes SendMail sent emails detected as spams (if using SendMail). Another and best option is to use SMTP as email engine. You can use Gmail or any other free SMTP service provider to use SMTP email engine.


u200b
If you are using your hosting smtp or any other provider smtp service then check their documentation for smtp settings.

Gmail SMTP configuration -

To configure gmail account first you have to create app password for SMTP service, Please check following steps to generate app password-

  1. Go to your Google Account.
  2. On the left navigation panel, choose Security.
  3. On the 'Signing in to Google' panel, choose App passwords. If you don’t see this option:
  • 2-Step Verification is not set up for your account
  • 2-Step Verification is set up for security keys only
  • Your account is through work, hospital or other organization
  • You’ve turned on Advanced Protection for your account
  1. At the bottom, choose Select app and choose the app that you’re using.
  2. Choose Select device and choose the device that you're using.
  3. Choose Generate.
  4. Follow the instructions to enter the app password. The app password is the 16-character code in the yellow bar on your device.
  5. Choose Done.

After generating gmail app password for SMTP service enter credentials in Smart Hospital SMTP email configuration-

Email Engine = SendMail/SMTP
SMTP Username = your gmail email id
SMTP Password = Generated App Password
SMTP Server = smtp.gmail.com
SMTP Port = 587
SMTP Security = TLS
SMTP Auth = ON

Note: After configuring email setting please check you have enabled email notification settings from Setup > Settings > Notification Setting.

5.21 About Billing

Vendor article · category: Billing · Mon, 01 Nov, 2021 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/about-billing

In Smart Hospital there is a feature of centralized billing so hospital staff not need to go to each module to generate patient bill individually for individual modules.

In centralized Billing module there are two ways to generate patient bill -

  • One is for single module (like Appointment, OPD, Pathology, Radiology etc) which purpose where patient comes for a particular treatment like patient had came for only blood test so in this case staff need to only generate their blood test bill which it can generate from Pathology tab.
  • Second one is for a billing of multiple treatments of patients under OPD / IPD which can be generate through a Case ID of patient.

We will understand through an example, suppose a patient come to hospital for their treatment and referred to OPD. Here doctors do checkups and give prescription to patient in which doctor prescribed some medicine and pathology and radiology tests for patient. Now patient go through some radiology and pathology tests and purchased some medicine. Now after test reports doctor suggest patient to admit in the hospital for further treatments so here patient IPD record will be create and doctor will do further treatments which may include some more pathology, radiology tests, operations and medications. So for billing of all these treatments in one go OPD/IPD Billing Through Case Id feature is very useful, here staff only need a Patient Case ID so patient all treatments will reflect.

5.36 About QR Code Attendance

Vendor article · category: QR Code Attendance · Sat, 16 Aug, 2025 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/about-qr-code-attendance

About QR Code / Barcode Attendance

**QR Code / Barcode Attendance:**To each Staff assigned a unique QR code / Barcode that represents their identity. These QR Code / Barcode can be generated from the certificate module of our Smart Hospital and this code usually contains information about the individual, such as a unique identifier.

  • QR code / Barcode are seamlessly integrated into the and staff ID cards additionally, individuals can conveniently access their QR codes / Barcodes through their dedicated and staff profiles.
  • To mark attendance, an organizer or instructor uses a QR code scanner.
  • Staff present their QR Code / Barcode to be scanned upon entry.
  • The scanner reads the code, and attendance data is recorded in the system.
  • Attendance records are updated in real-time, providing accurate and timely information.
  • This data accessed by administrators for tracking and reporting purposes.
  • Administrators gain seamless access to this data, empowering them for comprehensive tracking and insightful reporting.

5.38 How to add holiday in annual calendar on smart hospital?

Vendor article · category: Annual Calendar · Thu, 05 Sep, 2024 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/how-to-add-holiday-in-annual-calendar-on-smart-hospital

To add a holiday to the annual calendar, go to the Annual Calendar module in your Smart Hospital system and click on it. The Annual Calendar page will open on the right side.

Now go to the Add button, showing at the top right corner and click on it, Add window will be open In this window, you can see options for Type: Holiday, Activity, and Vacation. Simply select 'Holiday' by clicking on it, then choose the date when the holiday will occur. Add a description of the holiday, and if you want to display this holiday with details on the front site of your Smart Hospital, click on the 'Front Site' button. 

Finally, click the 'Save' button to save your holiday details in the holiday list.

To edit the holiday details simply go to the pencil icon showing at the right side and click on it, edit holiday window will be open

Now update the details you want to change, then click the 'Save' button. Your holiday details will be updated successfully.

To delete the holiday details, simply click on the delete icon on the right side, then click the 'OK' button. The holiday details will be deleted successfully

Then click on Search, in below list only display the holiday details.

Additionally you can also see the holiday details on the front site of your Smart Hospital, as you enabled this option when adding the holiday. Simply go to the front site of your Smart Hospital and navigate to the annual calendar

Here you can see the holiday details which you recently added from the annual calendar

You can see the holiday details on the calendar in both the superadmin and patient logins.

For Superadmin login, you can see a calendar icon at the top right corner. Click on it to open the calendar, where you can view the holiday details for the specific day you added

For patient login, you can see a calendar icon at the top right corner. Click on it to open the calendar, where you can view the holiday details for the specific day you added

5.39 How to create a Survey Form?

Vendor article · category: Survey Form · Sat, 25 Jul, 2026 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/how-to-create-a-survey-form

Go to Survey Forms → Survey Forms from the sidebar and click on the + Create Survey Form button on the top right of the list page.

On the Create Survey Form page, enter the Form Title, an optional Description shown above the form fields, and a Thank You Message shown to the user after they submit — leave the thank you message blank to show a default message instead.

Under Schedule, you can optionally set a Start Date and End Date so the form is only open for a limited period. Under Target Audience, select at least one of Staff, Patient or Front Site — this decides who will see the form once it is published.

Two more settings are available under Settings:

  • Allow Edit Response — lets a user who already submitted the form resubmit it, overwriting their previous answers.
  • Enable CAPTCHA — adds a security code verification step on public form submissions.

Click Save as Draft once you are done. The form is created in Draft status and you are taken straight to the Edit page, where the Survey Builder unlocks so you can start adding fields.

Note: a form needs at least one Target Audience selected, and at least one field added, before it can be Published.

Vendor article · category: TPA Management · Wed, 10 Nov, 2021 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/tpa-management

TPA module is for managing third party administrator or Mediclaim insurance provider companies. A third-party administrator is a company that provides operational services such as claims processing and employee benefits management under contract to another company. Insurance companies and self-insured companies often outsource their claims processing to third parties. With the help of TPA patient can get lots of discount in hospital charges.

To check TPA list associated with the hospital, login from superadmin, admin panel and then click on the TPA Management link present in the the left sidebar, by clicking this link you can check all TPA list.

added record will be show in TPA Management list page.

To see specific TPA charge details click on Organization Profile icon, for which you want to check tpa details, this will redirect you in details page, fro here you can check TPA charge details.

To check all details click on the Search button this will show you all charges.

Here you can edit or delete different associated charges for this TPA organization in different charge types. Associated charges should be applied first from hospital charges module.

Add TPA charges on hospital charges -

To add TPA charges on hospital charges, go to Setup > Hospital Charges, this will redirect you in Charges Details List page, here click on  +Add Charges button present at the top right corner of the page, then enter all mandatory details like Charge Type, Charge Category, Unit Type, Charge Name, Tax Category, Tax Category and Scheduled Charges For TPA (enter amount for different TPA) and then finally click on the Save button.

Once TPA amount is saved, you can use it in different module. For example you have added TPA for OPD charges, now when you add any opd charge you need to selected TPA and Charge Category, Charge and this will automatically calculated your TPA amount. For example your OPD consultation Fees was Rs.150 and you have select CGHS TPA for which opd consultation charge was Rs.100 so your applied charge will be Rs.100 .

You can also check patient details of allotted bed at mouse hover of bed icon or by click on bed icon, this will open IPD details of that patient.

You can also admit patient directly from Bed Status for available bed. For this is just click on available bed icon and add patient in IPD.

Floor

To add bed you need to first add Floor. To add Floor go to Setup > Bed > Floor, click on + Add Floor button and Name and Description for floor and click on Save button.

You can check this added record at Floor list page.

To edit Floor click on Edit icon and to delete section click on Delete icon present in the Floor  list.

Bed Group

You can add Bed Group to differentiate different ward on the same floor. To add Bed Group go to Setup > Bed > Bed Groupclick on Add Bed Group button, here enter Name, Floor, Color and Description for the Bed Group and click on Save button.

You can check this added record at Bed Group list page.

To edit Bed Group click on Edit icon and to delete section click on Delete icon present in the Bed Group list.

Bed Type

To add Bed Type go to Setup > Bed > Bed Type click on Add Bed Type button enter Name and click on Save button.

You can check this added record at Bed Type list page.

To edit Bed Type click on Edit icon and to delete section click on Delete icon present in the Bed Type  list.

Bed

To add bed go to Setup > Bed > Bed click on Add Bed button, here enter Name, Bed Type, Bed Group and Marked as unused (optional) and click on Save button.

You can check this added record at Bed list page.

To edit Bed click on Edit icon and to delete section click on Delete icon present in the Bed list.

5.51 404 Or Page Not Found Error In Installation

Vendor article · category: Common Issues & Troubleshooting · Mon, 18 Oct, 2021 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/404-or-page-not-found-error-in-installation

During installation if you are getting 404 or Page not found error then following possible causes may be behind this -

  1. Check .htaccess file is present in your Smart Hospital hosting directory. By default .htaccess files are hidden in cpanel, you can enable visible .(dot) hidden files from cpanel file manager setting option. .htaccess file already present in your downloaded package in respective folder.
  2. url rewriting module is disabled in your hosting.

5.52 Unable To Login Or Missing Login URL

Vendor article · category: Common Issues & Troubleshooting · Tue, 02 Nov, 2021 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/unable-to-login-or-missing-login-url

When you open Smart Hospital url then it will be open User Panel URL http://yourdomain/site/userlogin (if Front CMS is not enabled). By default Smart Hospital opens User Panel instead of Admin Panel (due to security reasons). 

In Smart Hospital your Admin Panel login url is http://yourdomain/site/login
Here superadmin, admin, doctor, accountant or any staff can be login through their email id and password.

And User Panel login is http://yourdomain/site/userlogin
Here only patient login through their username and password.

Please check you are login with right panel with right credentials.

5.53 ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY Issue On Server

Vendor article · category: Common Issues & Troubleshooting · Mon, 18 Oct, 2021 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/only_full_group_by-issue-on-server

If Smart Hospital showing ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY error message on your server that means on your hosting ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY is enabled in your mysql SQL_MODE. This issue comes due to on some hosting server mysql is not configured properly. Please contact to your hosting provider to disable/remove ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY in your hosting mysql SQL_MODE or follow the below instruction to fix this issue (it will require full root access of your mysql server) -

Open phpMyadmin of your server then go to Variables tab then edit sql mode variable value and remove ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY.

Note: This fix is temporary and if your mysql server will be restart or update it will comes on default state. So ask your hosting admin to make it permanently in mysql config file.

Generally this issue occurred in cheap or non professional hosting. If you will go with hosting providers like godaddy or hostgator or any reputed hosting provider then you will not face this issue.

5.54 Can I use special character in Smart Hospital?

Vendor article · category: FAQ · Mon, 18 Oct, 2021 · source: https://smart-hospital.in/article/can-i-use-special-character-in-smart-hospital

In Smart Hospital avoid to enter or using special character (special character is non-alphabetic and non-numeric like @, #, $, <, %, ^, &, *, !) for any field like Patient, Staff, Income, Expense, Transport, Custom Field etc, otherwise it may fail PHP or JavaScript processing.
